name: twincat-plc-toolkit
description: Structured Text editor, language server and project tools for Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 PLC projects: two-pane editor, offline IntelliSense and diagnostics, object and library explorers. Unofficial; not affiliated with Beckhoff.

tcToolkit.diagnostics.memberAccess.description: Flag access to members that do not exist on a resolved type (e.g. fb.NoSuchField).

tcToolkit.diagnostics.callArguments.description: Flag named call arguments that are not parameters of the resolved function/FB/method.

tcToolkit.diagnostics.declarationTypes.description: Flag declarations whose type is unknown. Off by default: types from library archives that cannot be read (the opaque .compiled-library-v3 format) are invisible to the indexer, so this may report false positives in projects that use them.

tcToolkit.diagnostics.typeCompatibility.description: Flag assignments whose value type is clearly incompatible with the target (e.g. assigning a struct to an INT).

tcToolkit.compiler.path.markdownDescription: Full path to the command-line file (`.cjs`) of an external IEC 61131-3 compiler for **TC Toolkit: Build Project** to run instead of the one that ships with the extension. Empty = the bundled compiler (the usual choice).

tcToolkit.compiler.nodePath.markdownDescription: Full path to a Node.js executable, version 22 or newer, that runs the compiler for **TC Toolkit: Build Project**. Empty = found automatically: `node` on `PATH`, then on Windows the usual install locations (Node.js installer, nvm-windows, Volta, fnm), then VS Code's own runtime when it is Node.js 22 or newer. The version is checked before each run.

tcToolkit.compiler.generateCpp.markdownDescription: **Generate C++.** After **TC Toolkit: Build Project** finds no errors, write the PLC project as C++ into a `CPP_Files` folder next to its `.plcproj` (beside `ST_Files`): `<project>.cpp` and `<project>.hpp`. Off by default. Turning off this setting also turns off `#tcToolkit.compiler.buildWithGpp#`. Only files TC Toolkit wrote there are ever replaced or deleted. Also in the Compile button's dropdown.

tcToolkit.compiler.buildWithGpp.markdownDescription: **Build with g++.** After the C++ is written, compile it with g++ (a compile check: `CPP_Files/<project>.o`, nothing is linked or run); g++'s errors appear in the Problems panel on the generated files. Optional: g++ is not needed for anything else. Turning this on also turns on `#tcToolkit.compiler.generateCpp#`. Off by default. Also in the Compile button's dropdown.

tcToolkit.compiler.gppPath.markdownDescription: Full path to the `g++` executable (`g++.exe` on Windows) that **Build with g++** runs. Empty = found automatically: `g++` on `PATH`, then on Windows the usual install folders (MSYS2 `ucrt64`/`mingw64`/`clang64`, `C:\MinGW`, WinLibs, w64devkit, Chocolatey's mingw). Filled with the g++ found when the build is turned on, if empty; a value you set is never overwritten. Run **TC Toolkit: Detect g++** to look again.

Filled automatically with the installation found on this machine; change it if yours is elsewhere. Empty = not found. Run **TC Toolkit: Detect XAE Shell Installations** to look again.

Filled automatically with the installation found on this machine; change it if yours is elsewhere. Empty = not found. Run **TC Toolkit: Detect XAE Shell Installations** to look again.

tcToolkit.xaeBuild.showWindow.markdownDescription: **Show the XAE window.** Show the XAE Shell window for the whole build instead of building headless. The window is always shown during activation, so a licence or download dialog can be answered, and it stays visible after an XAE version switch. Used by *TC Toolkit: Build through XAE* and *Build and Activate through XAE…* (Windows with TwinCAT XAE only).

tcToolkit.xaeBuild.configuration.markdownDescription: The solution configuration *Build through XAE* builds, normally `Release` or `Debug` (with the platform below, one of the pairs the solution declares). Free text, because a solution can declare its own configuration names.

tcToolkit.xaeBuild.platform.markdownDescription: The solution platform *Build through XAE* builds. Activating onto a runtime builds that runtime's platform: when the target runs another platform and the solution declares it, *Build and Activate through XAE…* offers to switch. A platform not in this list can still be typed into `settings.json`; the solution must declare it.

tcToolkit.xaeBuild.timeoutMinutes.markdownDescription: How many minutes a build through XAE may take before it is stopped (5 to 240). During activation it is extended once by 5 minutes and then only reported, never stopped.

tcToolkit.xaeBuild.stallMinutes.markdownDescription: Headless watchdog: after this many minutes without any output outside the build itself, offer to cancel and re-run with the window shown (2 to 60). A hidden XAE Shell can wait on a dialog nobody sees.

enumDescriptions: Ask every time which XAE Shell to use.
tcToolkit.libraryDefinitions.shell.markdownDescription: Which TwinCAT XAE Shell **Update Library Definitions** should drive. A library's signatures can differ between the 32-bit and 64-bit shell — visualisation libraries especially — so this defaults to asking. Set it if you always build with the same one. If the chosen shell is not installed, you are asked anyway rather than given the wrong signatures.

enumDescriptions: Through the TwinCAT AMS router on this PC (XAE or XAR installed; routes set up in XAE). The default.
Directly to the PLC over TCP, for a PC without TwinCAT. Needs the three direct settings below and a static route on the PLC to this PC. Never used unless chosen here.
tcToolkit.online.connectionMode.markdownDescription: **How Go Online reaches the PLC.** `router` (default) goes through the AMS router of the TwinCAT installation on this PC, using the routes you set up in XAE. `direct` connects to the PLC itself and is only for a PC without TwinCAT; it is never used as a fallback. Direct mode from a PC that also runs XAE can drop XAE's own connection to that PLC (one ADS connection per client address).

tcToolkit.online.adsPort.markdownDescription: **ADS port of the PLC runtime.** 851 is the first PLC runtime, 852 the second (850 + runtime number).

tcToolkit.online.routerAddress.markdownDescription: **AMS router address** (router mode). `127.0.0.1` is the router on this PC. Another address (for example, for Remote-SSH or WSL) is **untested**.

tcToolkit.online.direct.plcAddress.markdownDescription: **Direct mode: the PLC's IP address or host name.** Used only when `#tcToolkit.online.connectionMode#` is `direct`.

tcToolkit.online.direct.localAmsNetId.markdownDescription: **Direct mode: this PC's AMS Net ID**, as the PLC's static route to this PC names it (for example `192.168.1.20.1.1`). The route itself is created on the PLC or in XAE, never by this extension.

tcToolkit.online.direct.localAdsPort.markdownDescription: **Direct mode: the local ADS port** this PC uses (any free port; 32750 by default).

tcToolkit.online.allowWrites.markdownDescription: **Allow writing values.** Off by default, and only in your user settings: a workspace's settings cannot turn it on. When on, writes still have to be enabled once per online session, every write asks for a confirmation that names the target, the variable and the old and new values, and every write is logged to the *TC Toolkit Online* output channel. Writes are refused while the PLC runs a different project or an editor has unsaved edits, and from editors of a project the PLC does not run. A write sets the value once; it is not a force.

tcToolkit.online.inlinePollInterval.markdownDescription: **Inline values: refresh interval in milliseconds.** The visible variables are read with one batched read per interval.

tcToolkit.online.watchCycleTime.markdownDescription: **PLC Watch: notification cycle time in milliseconds.** Each watched variable is one on-change ADS notification checked at this cycle.

tcToolkit.online.maxNotifications.markdownDescription: **PLC Watch: the most ADS notifications at once.** Beckhoff recommends at most 550 per device; watched variables past this limit show no value until others are removed.
